guidance: Metrology aid for single-start 60° threads. The wires must be clean, straight and of the stated diameter, the micrometer calibrated, and the result compared with the thread's own pitch-diameter limits; the formula does not fit Acme, Whitworth or multi-start threads.
method: A 60° metric or unified thread has a basic profile height H = 0.866025P above the pitch line, so its basic pitch diameter is D − 2 × (3/8)H = D − 0.649519P, where D is the major diameter and P the pitch (1/TPI for a unified thread). A wire of diameter W resting in the groove touches the two flanks at a perpendicular distance W/2 from each, which puts its centre 2 × (W/2) = W from the sharp root apex along the groove bisector; the contact point on each flank is then 1.5W from the apex. With the micrometer across one wire on one side and two on the other, the reading is twice the centre distance plus twice the radius, M = D2 + 3W − 0.866025P, because the wire stack adds 3W while the root sits 0.866025P below the pitch diameter. The best wire is the one whose contact points land exactly on the pitch line: 1.5W = H/2 = 0.433013P, so W = 0.57735P, half the pitch times the secant of the 30° flank angle. Solving for a reading that was taken gives D2 = M + 0.866025P − 3W, the same as subtracting the constant 3W − 0.866025P printed on thread-wire charts, and that constant is shown with the result. Every error in the wire diameter enters the answer three times over, and the formula assumes a single-start thread with a low lead angle and no flank-angle error; it is the standard simplified form rather than the lead-angle-compensated one. A wire at or above 0.866025P bottoms out in the groove instead of seating on the flanks, so larger wires are refused. The page accepts a metric designation M<major>x<pitch> (M6x1, M10×1.5) or a unified one as a fraction, numbered size or decimal diameter with threads per inch (1/4-20 UNC, #10-24, 0.375-16); numbered sizes #0 to #12 take the ASME B1.1 series diameter 0.060 + 0.013n inch. Limits are 0.4 to 1,000 mm and 0.05 to 100 mm pitch for metric, 0.02 to 40 in and 1 to 400 TPI for unified. An optional reading and wire diameter accept a decimal point or comma and an optional matching unit; results are rounded to 0.001 mm or 0.0001 in, and the deviation is measured from the basic pitch diameter, not from a tolerance limit. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
